story_text.value:
Hey everyone,

I've always loved the simplicity of Go, but the only thing keeping me from switching all of my backends to Go is really one package, and one package only, which is Better-Auth. It's just so easy to use: simple plugin, and start working. It's got everything I need: organizations, teams, billing, social auth, everything.

I tried to scour GitHub and the open source community for anything remotely close to it in Go, and I honestly couldn't find anything that was worth it, so I just decided to make it myself. It's an open-source Go package. It is not 100% feature parity with Better-Auth yet, but it's getting there.

Would love some feedback. For anyone to try it out, it works with pretty much all of those routers: Chi, Echo, Fiber, Mux and more. Any feedback is greatly appreciated.

Oh, and it's also my very first open source repo, so I'm learning as I go.

title.value: Show HN: Plain-Auth an open-source authentication library for Go

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I’m building Codela to help coding agents learn from what happens after their code ships. I realized that my AI agent writes a change, the tests pass, and it gets deployed. Then in production a problem happens, I fix it, but what it did wrong and why never reaches the agent, so futures session usually make the same mistake.

So I built Codela which checks every deploy against how my app actually behaves in production (via my monitoring tool signoz) , learns from the ones that broke it, and teaches my agents so they don’t repeat the mistake.

Would love any feedback on this, thanks!

title.value: Show HN: I gave my AI Agents Production backed Memory

story_text.value:
Using Spawn, I've been building The Velvet Point, a rainy-night backgammon club you play in the browser (desktop or phone). You can play the house opponents or real people, and chat at the tables. You will also get analytical (as well as snarky) comments from the AI opponents. Social features, leaderboards (ratings, PR, chips) also baked in.

Has a review feature to show the best moves after your move. So no "hint" or tutoring before the move. I think you will learn better when you make a mistake - making a mistake will give your brain the feedback you need to learn better.

Uses gnubg's neural nets & bear-off tables in the background, ported to run in the browser. It's open source (https://github.com/ile/the-velvet-point).

Play here: https://www.spawn.co/@ilkkah/the-velvet-point

I'd love feedback. There may be bugs (hopefully just minor ones).

title.value: Show HN: A free browser backgammon club, gnubg's net under the hood

story_text.value:
I often use Codex/Claude for long-running tasks such as coding or video editing and hate it when it gets stuck while I’m away from my computer. I want a way to check in and operate my computer without being at my computer.

So I built ClawdTime. It FaceTimes me whenever it needs my input or has something to show me, and it zooms into the relevant window. I can also FaceTime it and have it run tasks on my Mac while it shares the screen.

All comments welcome!

story_text.value: With all the crazy math progress happening over last few months, I wanted to be able to understand it better so…. I worked with Claude (research), Gemini Neon (writing), and ChatGPT (images, narration) to make an ~8 hour audiobook and ebook that explores the discoveries, explains the math and, mostly importantly focuses on the human story and historical context of what’s been happening. It turned out quite good. Neon is the first model I’ve used where the writing is close to on par with very good human writing (with a few notable exceptions). Listening to it has been exhilarating. Also, the ebook version has full footnotes and references and is pretty much up to the minute as of today. Enjoy! And if you have ideas for the chapters of the next book / season, already in planning stages, please let me know.

title.value: Show HN: Free audiobook and eBook with the story of recent discoveries in math

story_text.value:
I'm Ilias, the creator behind Orcah Studio (a local-first knowledge system that will transcribe, perform speaker diarization, analyse frames, and create multi-modal embeddings) using open-weight models

Demo video: https://youtu.be/9uUZrayDEgs

I built a Docker-first solution, fully open source here: https://github.com/IliasHad/orcah-studio

Plus, a desktop app that will be plug-and-play with a richer video indexing pipeline. With integrations with DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, and Adobe Premiere Pro, and MCP tools (over 45 tools).

You can even link your videos with your Strava activities and extract camera metadata like ISO, Shutter Speed, Lens Model, and location, if available.

You can even do the same in your iPhone videos (index your videos in your videos, sync them with your Mac-indexed videos, so you can search them from your Mac or the other way). (Early alpha for now)

And even index videos on your Linux machine (alpha version) and use the macOS application as a client for that machine.

The goal is to make your videos indexable, searchable and most importantly, to build a memory from all your videos and connect the dots. Instead of just building a memory for a specific video, we can connect and link between all the videos that you have, without uploading anything to the cloud or paying us a subscription (one-time fee, no subscription fatigue or reminders haha)

Here's the macOS app that you can buy and start indexing your videos now: https://orcah.app

title.value: Show HN: A local-first AI memory for your video footage

story_text.value:
I recently became fascinated by the Europa Clipper mission, and it's multi planet journey all the way out to the orbit of Jupiter. With the close earth pass happening in just a few days, I thought it would be cool to visualize some of the amazing things its doing to get to Europa, and also be able to dive into some of the science behind what it's going to Europa for. The Launch Journey is the main storyline and focus of the site, but i've been adding some additional rooms and views, like diving into the individual parts of the ship or learning more about the radiation of Jupiter, etc.

I think the ability to interact with the thing you are learning about really helps make it interesting. Would love any thoughts or feedback!

title.value: Show HN: Journey To Europa: An interactive look at the Europa Clipper mission
